title: When the ZIA Terraform provider activates configuration

prose.text: ZIA stages configuration until it is activated, and the Terraform provider decides when to activate. {{activation-env-gate}} {{activation-call-selects-nothing}} {{activation-is-tenant-wide}}

checks.do: Whether a plan updated `zia_auth_settings_urls` when changes went live that nobody activated, before suspecting the platform.

activation-env-gate.statement: The ZIA provider's in-flight activation after a write runs only when the `ZIA_ACTIVATION` environment variable parses as true; otherwise the provider does not activate and the changes stay pending.

quotes: // Helper function to check if we should activate based on the ZIA_ACTIVATION environment variable
ZIA saves those changes into a pending state.
Set `ZIA_ACTIVATION=true` and the provider activates in-flight as resources are configured.

activation-call-selects-nothing.statement: The provider activates by posting an activation whose only field is a status of `ACTIVE`; the request names no particular change.

activation-is-tenant-wide.statement: So a provider activation publishes pending ZIA configuration, not only the change Terraform just wrote. The sources do not say whether pending changes are per admin or tenant-wide.
activation-is-tenant-wide.conditions: Inferred from the request having no change selection and from ZIA requiring an explicit activation for configuration changes.

quotes: For ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector APIs, configuration changes must be explicitly activated with a POST to /status/activate or /ecAdminActivateStatus/activate, respectively.

auth-settings-update-activates-ungated.statement: So an update of `zia_auth_settings_urls` activates whether or not `ZIA_ACTIVATION` is set, while its create activates only when the variable parses as true.
auth-settings-update-activates-ungated.conditions: Read from the whole update function, which has no shouldActivate call before triggerActivation, and from triggerActivation, which posts the activation without reading the variable; the provider does not state it.

only-unguarded-call.statement: Every other implicit activation (`triggerActivation` after a write) is guarded by `ZIA_ACTIVATION`: 220 guarded calls at v4.8.3 and 223 at the pin, with this update the only unguarded one at both. The explicit `zia_activation_status` resource activates unconditionally by design.
only-unguarded-call.conditions: Counted by scanning every resource file at v4.8.3 and HEAD for triggerActivation calls preceded within five lines by shouldActivate(); counts cannot be quoted.

update-publishes-unrelated-changes.statement: Updating `zia_auth_settings_urls` therefore publishes pending ZIA changes beyond its own, even when `ZIA_ACTIVATION` is unset and the operator expects changes to stay staged.

update-publishes-unrelated-changes.conditions: Chain of evidence: the update path activates unconditionally, and activation publishes every pending change in the tenant (the claims derived from). Not observed on a tenant.

activation-scope.title: Whether a ZIA activation publishes only the caller's pending changes or every admin's
activation-scope.blocks: saying whether an implicit activation can publish another admin's staged work
activation-scope.detail: Test with two API clients or admins: stage a change as each, activate as one, and check whether the other's change went live.
